title: Two businessmen accuse Utah Rep. Trevor Lee of past check fraud, abuse of power
text:
Videos posted on a website funded by a former employer allege that Utah Rep. Trevor Lee, R-Layton, committed check fraud more than a decade ago while working as
Videos posted on a website funded by a former employer allege that Utah Rep. Trevor Lee, R-Layton, committed check fraud more than a decade ago while working as a salesman for Moxie Pest Control.
Lee acknowledged past misconduct but called the timing politically motivated as he faces a Republican convention challenge.
“Please do not elect Trevor Lee to the State Legislature or, quite frankly, any position of public trust,” Walton said in one video.
Walton and his business partner alleged that Lee, while selling for the company in North Carolina, altered company checks by cashing them for more than their face value. Phil Nielsen, identified as Lee’s former supervisor, said a bookkeeper flagged irregularities involving multiple checks with Lee as the common factor. The bank identified the activity as check fraud, Nielsen said.
Nielsen said he and Walton confronted Lee, who initially denied involvement. Lee later admitted the behavior when told the matter could be referred to police, according to Nielsen. The company did not involve law enforcement but instead reached an agreement with Lee, which Walton has posted online.
Lee, who began serving in the Utah House in January 2023, is seeking re-election to District 16 in Davis County. He faces an intraparty challenge at the state Republican nominating convention in 10 days. He defeated a challenger at the 2024 convention and won the general election.
“I admitted my wrongdoing, made restitution, and vowed not to repeat the behavior,” Lee said. “That chapter is long closed, and I have spent every day since earning the trust of those I serve.”
Lee questioned the timing of the claims, noting multiple interactions with Walton over the past two years without prior issues raised. He described the accusations as a personal attack amid a campaign where opponents “can’t win on the issues.”
A separate video on the site features Trent Spafford, president and CEO of Utah water company Enevive. Spafford called Lee “dishonest” and alleged that several months ago Lee sought a $93,000 personal financial advance while suggesting he could help the company secure a government contract. That contract never materialized, Spafford said. He also accused Lee of making similar promises to another local water company.
Walton said he contacted Spafford and others months ago while researching Lee’s background. Walton said he was initially unaware Lee had run for office and only recently escalated his concerns after speaking with others.
“There’s never been a time in Utah or the United States of America when it was more important to take into account someone’s character when electing them to public office,” Walton said.
“We are carefully reviewing the matter and will follow the appropriate process to determine the facts and any next steps,” Schultz said. “Allegations of this nature involving a sitting legislator are taken seriously.”
“In my early 20’s, I made a grave error. I behaved dishonestly with my employer at the time, Mr. Jason Walton. I have deeply regretted my behavior at the time, more than a decade ago. I admitted my wrongdoing, made restitution, and vowed not to repeat the behavior. That chapter is long closed, and I have spent every day since earning the trust of those I serve. Now, for reasons that are not clear to me, Mr. Walton has decided to drag up this past incident in order to damage me politically. Even after many many different interactions over the last two years, with him never having an issue. Since first running for office four years ago, I have been a staunch conservative fighter for the people of Utah. I have made every effort to be transparent, accessible, and relentlessly focused on keeping our state the best in the country. My family has supported my efforts, sacrificing countless nights, weekends, and family time to answer every call, attend every event, and deliver results on the issues that matter most: protecting our freedoms, strengthening our economy, securing our borders, and fighting back against federal overreach. It is sad when campaigns resort to personal attacks when opponents can’t win on the issues. But I have never shied away from the truth, and I never will. I’m happy to talk to anyone, anytime, because my record of service speaks louder than any former lapse in judgment. My door is always open, my focus remains on Utah families, and my commitment to conservative values has never been stronger.”
